sections.nav_title: Follow the possession before the shot
sections.heading: Follow the possession before the shot
paragraphs: Start with the player holding the ball, then locate the rim. In this wide indoor view, several players remain visible around the action. Pause before release and identify who is directly involved in the play instead of following every moving person. Replay once at normal speed to reconnect that static arrangement with the actual movement.

sections.heading: Compare the two retained plays
paragraphs: The edit contains two selected shooting sequences rather than a complete game. Treat each sequence as its own observation: where is the shooter relative to the basket, when does the ball become visible, and when does the sequence end? A change between selected plays is an editing boundary, not evidence that the possessions happened back to back.

sections.heading: Keep the claims inside the frame
paragraphs: The clip does not establish the players’ names, the score, the result of the game or a shooting percentage. A visible trail helps follow the ball; it does not measure shot difficulty. If you make notes, describe observable actions and leave unknown game context blank.
